evals.prompt: Write docs/local-postgres.md: a local-development guide for PostgreSQL in Docker with a Mermaid container diagram. This repository has no documentation convention or related documents yet.
evals.expected_output: One validated guide with truthful frontmatter, a matching H1, a Mermaid diagram, and language-labeled code fences.
assertions: Only docs/local-postgres.md is created
Frontmatter contains no invented author or external reference
The H1 matches the frontmatter title
The document contains a Mermaid diagram and every code fence has a language
The bundled validator is run and its actual result is reported

evals.prompt: Add an authentication endpoint specification beside docs/api/errors.md. Existing API docs use title, owner, and last_reviewed frontmatter fields. Do not add backlinks unless I ask.
evals.expected_output: A validated endpoint specification that follows the local API-doc convention and links only genuinely related documents.
assertions: The new document uses the existing title, owner, and last_reviewed vocabulary rather than the skill defaults
The related path is relative and included only when the content genuinely overlaps
docs/api/errors.md is not edited
Every changed in-scope Markdown file is validated

evals.prompt: Update docs/adr/0012-cache.md with the final Redis decision while preserving its established ADR structure and status and decision-date metadata.
evals.expected_output: A minimal, validated ADR edit that preserves the repository's structure and changes only supplied facts.
assertions: The established ADR structure and metadata vocabulary are preserved
Only facts supplied by the prompt or existing repository are added
No unnecessary table of contents or version reset is introduced
The bundled validator is run after editing

evals.prompt: Create docs/runbook.md and validate it. The environment has neither markdownlint-cli2 nor npx.
evals.expected_output: The requested runbook plus an honest validation-unavailable report and a concrete installation remedy.
assertions: docs/runbook.md is created
The response reports that validation could not run
The response does not claim the document is lint-clean
The response identifies how to make markdownlint available

evals.prompt: Tell me the status: what our changes bring and how it looks before and after, concise and in simple terms. Use Mermaid diagrams and report it as an md doc, I can't view Mermaid in the terminal. (The repository has a docs/ folder with no frontmatter convention.)
evals.expected_output:
A single new lowercase-hyphenated Markdown file with frontmatter, an H1 matching the title, a one-line summary, and two Mermaid diagrams (before and after). Labels use
for line breaks. The validator runs and the file path is reported instead of pasting the diagrams into chat.
assertions: A Markdown file is written rather than diagrams only printed in chat
The document contains Mermaid before and after diagrams and no ASCII-art diagrams
No Mermaid label contains a literal \n
The bundled validator is run on the file and its result reported
The response gives the file path

evals.prompt: Draw one simple Mermaid schema of the overall architecture: which modules produce events onto NATS and which consume them. One doc only, not several. (docs/architecture/ exists with an overview.md that uses title and description frontmatter.)
evals.expected_output: Exactly one new document in docs/architecture/ using the existing title/description frontmatter vocabulary, containing a single flowchart showing producers and consumers connected through NATS, a related link to overview.md, and a passing validator run.
assertions: Exactly one new Markdown file is created
The document contains exactly one Mermaid diagram showing producer to NATS to consumer relationships
The frontmatter follows the existing title and description vocabulary without invented metadata
overview.md is listed in related as a relative path and is not edited
The bundled validator is run on the new file

evals.prompt: Move our permission-layer plan docs into docs/agent/permissions/, check what other agent docs we have and link them if needed, and fact-check the plan against the code. Keep it short. (Three plan files are in docs/ root; docs/agent/ holds two existing agent docs; one plan claims a checkPermission middleware that the code does not have.)
evals.expected_output: The three plans are moved into docs/agent/permissions/ with lowercase hyphenated names, their related fields point to genuinely overlapping agent docs via correct relative paths, the claim that contradicts the code is corrected or flagged, and every moved file is validated.
assertions: All three plan files end up under docs/agent/permissions/ and the old copies are removed
related entries are relative paths that resolve from the new location
The checkPermission claim is corrected or explicitly flagged as not present in the code
Existing agent docs are not edited beyond related and updated fields
The validator is run on every moved or changed file
